description:
#AD When you use loyalty points to unlock an upgrade or a holiday, your brain releases dopamine! Dopamine is responsible for making you feel excited about something, that’s why saving feels so good.

I’ve teamed up with @virginred to explore how British buyers’ brains light up when they save, and why unlocking rewards through loyalty points gives such a powerful buzz.

#dopamine #neuroscience #brainhealth #selfdevelopment #habits #rewireyourbrain
transcript: Have you ever noticed how saving money feels like a high? That's because of dopamine. I teamed up with Virgin Red to see what happens in people's brains and how they light up in response to saving on a purchase. Here are the results and the science. Every time you spend points on a flight, a hotel, or even an upgrade, your brain's reward system lights up. Dopamine doesn't just fire up when you get an unexpected reward, it also lights up in anticipation of a reward. This means that when you know you're saving money, your brain already gets a feel good hit. And here's the best part, when you experience an unexpected saving much bigger than you originally thought, your brain releases even more dopamine in response to that. Research shows that 85% of Brits get a buzz from saving and nearly 1 in 4 get an even bigger buzz when they know that they're spending loyalty points. the biggest highs come from smart wins like bagging an upgrade or spending loyalty points on something that you really really really needed without even spending a penny so the next time you treat yourself using virgin points remember it's not just a smart move but it's your brain's dopamine being released before the trip even starts
